A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EHR2Path on MIMIC-IV. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original next-hour prediction, longitudinal simulation, outcome fine-tuning and ablation results in Tables 1–5, with a qualitative simulation in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original forecasting, simulation, fine-tuning and ablation results in Tables 1–5, plus performance across forecast horizons in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The hierarchical EHR representation, three model variants, masked summarization, LOS indicator and two fine-tuning strategies are retained. V2 clarifies 24-hour inputs and reuse of predicted LOS during inference; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use MIMIC-IV 2.2 across ED, hospital wards and ICU for the same development and outcome tasks. The explicit MIMIC-IV-ED/Note links identify already-used data, and the three-day ICU stay/discharge endpoint remains matched. The horizon analysis stays within existing forecast coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the statistical baseline and ETHOS for next-step prediction, ETHOS for applicable simulations, and MEME/REMed for outcome prediction. Newly discussed related-work models are not added evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation at four-hour forecast-horizon increments. It also states no exclusions instead of minimal exclusions and restates the ICU target from remaining beyond three days to discharge within three days. Splits, sample counts and main metrics are retained; these wording revisions do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 adds a systematic horizon-sensitivity analysis across five development tasks, with eight event-F1/value-MAE panels in Figure 5. This tests deterioration during iterative forecasting, beyond v1's retained LOS and bottleneck-size ablations and qualitative vital-sign example.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without run-count or uncertainty information. V2 adds 95% confidence intervals to model results in Tables 1–3 and confidence bands in Figure 5; Appendix A.4 identifies single-run results with bootstrapped intervals. This expands uncertainty reporting without demonstrating additional training runs.

E6.justification: Central results are revised: Table 1 changes E2P-S macro F1 from 0.54 to 0.48 and combined-model average/maximum input tokens from 220/1494 to 1585/5744. Table 2 changes hospital-medication F1 from 0.73/0.72 to 0.83/0.82 for text/summary models. Table 3 changes REMed mortality accuracy from 0.78 to 0.71, reversing its ranking against pathway fine-tuning. Figure 5 adds horizon-dependent results.

T1.justification: The temporal representation, summary-token definitions, attention-mask equation and information-bottleneck reasoning are retained. V2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation, proof or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The core forecasting and summarization contributions remain. V2 drops the 'first holistic pathway foundation model' assertion and the claim of natural extension to long-term pathways, emphasizing retrospective in-hospital forecasting and performance on directly comparable tasks.

C2.justification: V2 interprets horizon degradation as gradual rather than catastrophic. It also narrows the summary model's numerical advantage to the micro score and replaces the blanket fewer-input-tokens interpretation with a context–efficiency tradeoff. The single-healthcare-system limitation remains, in shortened form.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code URL, explicit ED/Note data links, hourly mean/mode aggregation, decoding parameters, 18-category diagnosis details and clearer LOS inference instructions. Most training and hardware details are retained, while v1's explicit 65/24-step ablation convergence limits disappear.

R1.justification: The positioning becomes substantially more EHR-specific: UniHPF, GenHPF, ESGPT, CEHR-GPT and MOTOR are added and contrasted with EHR2Path. Broad general-LLM and medical-chat background is removed, and the categorical 'first' foundation-model positioning is softened.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around in-hospital clinical forecasting and three explicit contributions. Related work and results discussions are substantially revised, task/model terminology is clarified, and Appendices A–E become Sections A.1–A.5.

P2.justification: V2 adds evaluation radar charts, an eight-panel horizon figure and a task-definition table; revises Figure 1 and the output example; and restructures results tables to display intervals. A new document template changes typography and layout. The original qualitative simulation remains, renumbered as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the evidence easier to assess through confidence intervals, horizon analysis, more accurate combined-model token accounting and clearer inference/task documentation. Its narrower in-hospital positioning better matches the experiments. These gains are tempered by unexplained score revisions and removal of explicit ablation stopping limits, supporting a limited overall improvement.
